summary: Gossan is the Hearthian flight instructor and zero-g coach for Outer Wilds Ventures, stationed at the entrance to the Zero-G Cave on Timber Hearth. They are one of the OWV founding members and run the player's pre-launch ship-repair tutorial.

biology: Gossan is missing one eye and part of their left ear.
Gossan appears with all four eyes in the inaugural Outer Wilds founders' photo, indicating their eye loss occurred after OWV was founded.
behavior: Gossan urges the Protagonist to attempt the Zero-G Cave satellite repair before the launch.
Gossan clashes with Slate over safety features on the spaceships.
Gossan made Slate install a safety harness in the cockpit despite Slate's objection about thrust-to-weight ratios.
Gossan tells the Protagonist not to get killed after they have invested training time.
location: Gossan is located at the entrance to the Zero-G Cave on Timber Hearth, near the Observatory.
Gossan crashed into the Attlerock on their first piloted trip.
lore: Gossan is one of the founders of Outer Wilds Ventures.
Gossan is the player's flight instructor and zero-g coach.
Gossan previously piloted a ship but ended their piloting career after crashing into the Attlerock.
Gossan used to work closely with Slate (the engineer) and Feldspar (the best pilot) in OWV's early days.
Gossan was known as the 'Zero-G Coach' during the game's alpha.
Gossan presents the Zero-G Cave's broken mining equipment as a 'satellite' for the training exercise.
Gossan told Arkose that the patch of Ghost Matter in the village was bigger when Gossan was a hatchling.
Porphy and Gossan exchange clearly visible flirtations, observed by Esker via signalscope from the Attlerock.
Porphy suggests opening 'The Good Stuff' with the Protagonist and Gossan after the flight.
Hornfels and Gossan are the primary ground control contacts; Esker mentions they radio up to chat.
Slate cites Gossan's Zero-G training exercise as something the Protagonist's practice run would 'help get Gossan off my back' about.
Slate says only Gossan would worry about the ship's log destination markers possibly shorting out the fuel regulator.
Gossan told Mica that if Mica ever designs a faster ship than Slate's, Mica should ask Slate to be the first test pilot.
Feldspar worked more closely with Gossan and Slate than with Hornfels in OWV's history.
Feldspar's journal about reaching the core of Giant's Deep notes their eagerness to tell Gossan and Hornfels.
If the Protagonist tells Hornfels where Feldspar is, Hornfels plans to have Gossan prepare a ship to retrieve them.
The Self ending implies that both the Protagonist and Slate had some involvement in Gossan's eye-loss incident.
The Self ending cites the eye-loss incident as a reason Gossan and Slate never dated.
Self notes that Gossan, unlike Slate, considers a date going well when two people are talking and nothing has exploded yet.
mechanics: Speaking to Gossan unlocks the Zero-G Cave satellite-repair tutorial, which teaches ship-repair mechanics in zero gravity with the Spacesuit.
The Zero-G Cave is accessed via an elevator near Gossan's position.
Completing the satellite repair sends the player to retrieve launch codes from the Observatory.
